Aisha Patel: Hey team — new shadow thread. I'm shadowing Tom this weekend for on-call handoff + incident runthroughs. Wanted to confirm primary/secondary and surface a small coverage gap I noticed.
Tom Nguyen: Thanks Aisha. I'll be primary Sat 00:00-12:00 UTC, Miguel is secondary Sat 00:00-24:00 UTC, and I'm primary again Sun 00:00-12:00 UTC. Quick note: there's currently no assigned secondary for Sun 12:00-24:00 UTC. We should either split Miguel's shift or find a volunteer.
Miguel Santos: I can extend into Sun 12:00-18:00 UTC if needed, but need coverage 18:00-24:00. Anyone can take the late slot?
Priya Kapoor: I can swap some hours — I can cover Sun 18:00-24:00 UTC but would prefer being tagged as backup only. I'm in APAC so late evening is ok for me.
Aisha Patel: Perfect — thanks Priya. So current plan: Tom primary Sat/Sun mornings, Miguel Sat full and Sun morning+afternoon, Priya backup Sun late. I'll shadow Tom Sat morning and Miguel Sat evening to see handoff flows.
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident page test scheduled — reminder: run through the mitigation checklist at least once during your shadow shift. (Incident ID: TEST-2026-01)
Tom Nguyen: For the runbook walkthrough, please follow the "Incident Triage -> Pager Response" steps here: https://internal.runbooks.redwood/oncall/pager-response . Key commands we use:
```
# check active incidents
rwctl incidents list --status active
# tail prod logs for request ID
kubectl logs -n prod -l app=api --tail=200 | rg "<request-id>"
# escalate to SRE manager
pagerduty trigger --service=sre-team --dedup="$INCIDENT_ID"
```
Aisha Patel: Got it. During the shadow I want to watch: alert verification, initial impact assessment (customers/regions), deciding rollback vs mitigation, comms template. Tom, can you demo the initial triage on a small test alert during Sat morning?
Tom Nguyen: Absolutely. I'll fire a staged alert at 08:30 UTC (non-prod alert channel) and walk through the steps. We'll simulate customer impact: partial latency increase in eu-west-1. Please note the shortcut for quick severity update in our incident chat: `/severity P1` or `/severity P2` in the incident channel.
Miguel Santos: Heads up — when you check services, watch the cache hit rates. Last month an evict storm caused latency spikes; cache metrics are at https://grafana.internal/d/cache-metrics-dashboard. If you see cache_miss_rate > 0.12 for >5m, consider warming caches or temporarily routing reads to the replica pool.
Priya Kapoor: Also flag the KV cache keyspace and check the KV cache health playbook section: https://internal.runbooks.redwood/oncall/kv-cache . It's one of our frequent triage items.
SRE Manager: One operational note — if the incident looks like customer impact > 10% or cross-region, escalate to SEV2 immediately and loop in the platform PMs via the incident checklist. Paging matrix is here: https://internal.runbooks.redwood/oncall/paging-matrix
Aisha Patel: For handoffs, let's keep this checklist in the thread so I can reference during shadow:
- Confirm primary/secondary names + contact methods
- Review active incidents and any mitigations in progress
- Run a quick smoke test for critical user flows
- Share any scheduled deploys or maintenance for next 12h
- Confirm alert thresholds changed during the shift
Tom Nguyen: I exported the current on-call rota to my drive and pasted the relevant block into the team calendar. Reminder command to fetch rota:
```
rwctl rota current --service inference-platform --format table
```
Miguel Santos: If someone gets paged and can't respond within 5 minutes, handoff to the secondary and annotate in the incident chat with `//handoff reason` so we keep the timeline clean.
Priya Kapoor: Quick onboarding tasks for Aisha while shadowing:
1) Run through one full triage with me or Tom (in non-prod) — validate your access and PD escalation flow
2) Execute the mitigation playbook: cache-warming and short-term rate-limiting
3) Practice declaring a severity and posting the customer-impact blurb
4) Confirm you can open bridge and add notes to incident timeline
Aisha Patel: Thanks — I'll tick those off. One more question: what's our threshold for involving the Dedicated infra team vs SRE on calls? I remember something about GPU pool impact having a different path.
SRE Manager: Good question. If the incident is isolated to dedicated GPU pools (resource exhaustion, node OOMs), page eng-infra and ENG-PLATFORM channel and tag `@infra-oncall`. For user-facing latency or correctness issues, SRE leads the response and pulls infra as needed. The decision tree is in the runbook: "dedicated-vs-platform-escalation" (https://internal.runbooks.redwood/oncall/dedicated-escalation)
Tom Nguyen: Final practical note for Aisha: bring a laptop with your SSH key loaded and have your PagerDuty set to mobile push + email. We use short 5-min escalations for P1 during weekends.
Aisha Patel: Copy that. I'll be online 06:30-16:30 UTC Sat pairing with Tom and then shadow Miguel 20:00-00:00 UTC. If anyone needs to DM me during that window: @Aisha (Slack) or pagerduty Aisha_Patel.
Miguel Santos: Thanks — I'll create a quick checklist doc and drop it in the shadowing folder: https://files.internal/shadowing/oncall-aisha-2026.md
Priya Kapoor: One last small tip: if you need to mute noisy non-prod alerts while testing, use `rwctl alerts mute --label test=true --duration 30m` so you don't get double-paged.
oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Reminder: Runbook practice completed? Mark done with `/runbook complete TEST-2026-01` in the channel.
Aisha Patel: Will do. Thanks everyone — appreciate the onboarding support. I'll post any notes and screenshots from the shadow session here after the staged alert.
Tom Nguyen: See you at 08:30 UTC. I'll ping the test alert then. :thumbsup:
